learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Omission is available and is not scored as a selected misconception.

items.title: Starting check: gonadal function
items.prompt: Which paired function is most directly associated with the testes?
options: Sperm production and androgen secretion
Sperm maturation and long-term uterine support
Oocyte transport and implantation support
Semen delivery and ovarian hormone secretion
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Guided practice: maturation before transport
items.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes epididymis and vas deferens?
options: The vas deferens produces sperm; the epididymis produces testosterone
The epididymis supports sperm maturation; the vas deferens transports sperm
The epididymis supports implantation; the vas deferens transports oocytes
Both structures are ovarian hormone-producing gonads
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Less help: fertilization site
items.prompt: Which structure most commonly transports the oocyte and provides the usual site of fertilization?
options: Uterus
Cervix
Oviduct
Vagina
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: On your own: implantation support
items.prompt: Which structure directly provides the site for implantation and supports prenatal development?
options: Epididymis
Vas deferens
Oviduct
Uterus
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Near exit: compare gonads
items.prompt: Which comparison of ovaries and testes is correct?
options: Both produce gametes and secrete reproductive hormones
Both serve primarily as ducts for mature gametes
Ovaries support implantation while testes support fertilization
Testes produce oocytes while ovaries produce sperm
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Changed exit: separate transport and secretion
items.prompt: A vas deferens is experimentally blocked while testicular tissue remains functional. Which direct outcome is most likely?
options: Sperm production stops completely while androgen secretion rises sharply
Sperm transport into the ejaculate falls while androgen secretion can continue
Oocyte transport through an oviduct stops while uterine support continues
Implantation stops because the uterine lining and cervix are both absent
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair shared gonadal functions
items.prompt: Which description correctly identifies the two shared functions of ovaries and testes?
options: Both are primarily transport ducts and neither secretes hormones
Both support implantation and serve as the usual fertilization site
Both produce gametes and secrete reproductive hormones
Both mature sperm and store oocytes after ovulation
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: separate gonadal roles
items.prompt: A research model preserves hormone-secreting cells in both ovaries and testes but disables gamete-forming cells. Which shared gonadal function is directly lost?
options: Transport through the oviduct and vas deferens
Support of implantation by both gonads
Secretion of every reproductive hormone by both gonads
Production of oocytes or sperm, respectively
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair disruption tracing
items.prompt: How should a localized duct blockage be analyzed?
options: Locate the duct step, then preserve unaffected upstream functions
Assume every reproductive production, transport, and endocrine function stops
Convert the obstructed transport duct into a hormone-producing gonad
Infer a specific clinical diagnosis solely from the structure's name
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: oviduct transport
items.prompt: An oviduct is blocked while ovarian cycling remains intact. Which direct prediction is strongest?
options: Ovarian hormone secretion and follicular cycling must immediately stop
Gamete meeting is impaired while ovarian endocrine cycling can continue
The vas deferens begins transporting the oocyte toward the uterus
The uterus becomes the usual fertilization site after oviduct blockage
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Starting check: axis direction
items.prompt: Which sequence correctly represents the initial hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal signal path?
options: LH → posterior pituitary → gonadal hormones
FSH → hypothalamus → GnRH and insulin
GnRH → anterior pituitary → FSH and LH
Progesterone → thyroid → GnRH and FSH
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Guided practice: male gonadal targets
items.prompt: Which pairing correctly describes major LH and FSH functions in the testes?
options: LH supports Sertoli cells; FSH produces adrenal cortisol
LH transports sperm; FSH stores sperm in the epididymis
LH triggers menstruation; FSH supports uterine implantation
LH stimulates Leydig testosterone; FSH supports Sertoli function
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Less help: follicular development
items.prompt: During the follicular phase, which change most directly follows increased FSH action?
options: Follicular development with increasing estrogen production
Immediate uterine implantation of an embryo
Corpus-luteum regression and progesterone withdrawal
Permanent suppression of all ovarian activity
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: On your own: ovulatory trigger
items.prompt: Which hormonal event most directly triggers ovulation?
options: A sustained fall in all gonadotropins
A midcycle LH surge
A progesterone drop before follicle growth
A gradual decline in follicular estrogen
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Near exit: hormone withdrawal
items.prompt: Without pregnancy-maintaining signals, the corpus luteum regresses. Which sequence is expected?
options: FSH and LH disappear permanently from circulation
Progesterone rises continuously and menstruation stops
Progesterone and estrogen fall, then menstruation follows
Testosterone rises and directly maintains the endometrium
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Changed exit: switch the feedback sign
items.prompt: Estrogen remains high for a sustained interval near midcycle. Which response is most likely?
options: Negative feedback eliminates LH and prevents ovulation
FSH permanently suppresses all follicular development
Progesterone withdrawal immediately causes menstruation
Positive feedback produces an LH surge and promotes ovulation
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair the luteal transition
items.prompt: After corpus-luteum regression without a pregnancy-maintaining signal, which causal sequence should be used?
options: Progesterone and estrogen fall → endometrial support decreases → menstruation follows
Progesterone rises → the endometrium is maintained indefinitely → menstruation follows
LH disappears permanently → the corpus luteum enlarges → ovulation repeats
Testosterone rises → endometrial support increases → menstruation stops
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: end-of-cycle withdrawal
items.prompt: At the end of a nonpregnant cycle, luteal tissue loses support and progesterone falls. Which transition is expected next?
options: A new LH surge immediately triggers a second ovulation
Endometrial support decreases and menstruation begins
The corpus luteum enlarges and progesterone rises again
Testosterone replaces progesterone as the endometrial signal
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair feedback-sign selection
items.prompt: Which cue marks the positive-feedback exception in the ovarian cycle?
options: Progesterone withdrawal after luteal regression
Low estrogen during early follicular recruitment
Sustained high estrogen near midcycle
Ordinary gonadal negative feedback outside midcycle
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: late-follicular feedback
items.prompt: During the late follicular phase, an experiment sustains high estradiol while progesterone remains low. Which phase-specific response is expected?
options: Negative feedback suppresses LH completely and prevents any ovulatory signal
Progesterone withdrawal immediately initiates menstruation
FSH permanently shuts down all follicular development
Positive feedback promotes an LH surge that supports ovulation
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.
